Follow these 4 steps once (about 1 minute). Steps get a check mark automatically.
Open About phone and tap \"Build number\" 7 times. Skip if already on.
Connect to Wi-Fi first. In Developer options, turn on Wireless debugging and tap Allow if asked.
Tap the button below. Then open Wireless debugging and tap \"Pair device with pairing code\". Keep that dialog open, pull down the notification shade, tap \"Enter code\" and type the 6 digits.
Allow notifications, then tap Start pairing again
Connects by itself after pairing. Tap if it does not.
All set! Go back to see per-app CPU and RAM.
Show network and temperature on popup bubble
The status bar icon shows one metric. Pull down the notification shade to see all of them.
Only used during setup to read the pairing code in Settings and pair automatically. Nothing is collected or sent.
Turn on SysWidget in Accessibility, then come back and tap Auto pair
Tap Auto pair. The app opens Wireless debugging and pairs by itself. First time it asks you to enable SysWidget in Accessibility.
Per-app CPU/RAM needs a connection. Open the Connect tab.
Per-app GPU is not provided by Android.
Per-core data needs a connection (Connect tab).
Plug the phone into a PC with USB debugging on and run: adb tcpip 5555 . Then tap Connect and choose \"Always allow\" on the phone. Lasts until reboot.

1) Tap Start pairing (opens Wireless debugging). 2) Tap \"Pair device with pairing code\" and keep that dialog open. 3) Pull down the notification shade, tap \"Enter code\" and type the 6 digits (Android hides floating windows over the pairing screen). Fields below are for manual entry.
Port found: %1$d. Now type the 6-digit code.
Allow SysWidget to show a floating Task Manager over other apps. Everything (stats, charts, per-app usage, connection) is inside the popup.
Display over other apps: not allowed yet
Tap the small bubble to expand it. In the popup, the Connect tab sets up per-app CPU/RAM.
On Android 11 or above, you can enable Wireless debugging and connect directly from your device, without a computer.\n\nPlease view the step-by-step guide first.
Start by connecting to a computer
Plug the phone into a computer and run one adb command. This needs to be repeated every time the device restarts.

On the computer (USB debugging on), run:

%1$s

Then come back and tap Start. Choose "Always allow" on the phone.

1. Connect to Wi-Fi.
2. Turn on Developer options (tap Build number 7 times in About phone).
3. Tap Pairing here. Allow notifications if asked.
4. In Wireless debugging, turn it on, then tap "Pair device with pairing code" and keep the dialog open.
5. Pull down the notification shade, tap "Enter pairing code" and type the 6 digits.
6. When it says connected, you are done. Tap Start if it does not connect by itself.
The pairing process needs you to interact with a notification from SysWidget. Please allow SysWidget to post notifications.
Wireless debugging is opening. Turn it on, tap \"Pair device with pairing code\" and keep that dialog open. Then pull down the notification shade and tap \"Enter pairing code\".
Per-app CPU/RAM needs Shizuku. Open the connection screen to check and grant permission.
Paired, but could not connect: %1$s. Keep Wi-Fi and Wireless debugging on, then open ADB connection and tap Start.
SysWidget uses Shizuku to read per-app CPU/RAM, GPU and FPS. Install and start Shizuku, then grant SysWidget permission.

1. Install Shizuku (tap Get Shizuku).
2. Open Shizuku and choose "Start via Wireless debugging": enable Developer options and Wireless debugging, tap Pairing, enter the code from the notification, then tap Start. (Or start it from a computer.)
3. Come back here and tap Grant permission.
4. Status turns green. Open the Processes tab in the popup.
